title: Marble Floor Restoration in Business Bay: What to Expect
h1: Marble Floor Restoration in Business Bay: What to Expect
description: How marble wears in Business Bay towers and offices, what restoration involves, and how to plan the work around building rules and busy hours.
excerpt: How marble wears in Business Bay towers and offices, and how to plan restoration around building rules and busy hours.
intro: Marble in a Business Bay tower works hard. Lobbies, lift halls and office corridors see heavy foot traffic every day, and apartments pick up sand from balconies and busy streets. This guide explains what restoration involves in a tower, and how to plan it with the least disruption.

sections.h2: How marble wears in a tower
body: Tower floors usually fail in the same places.

• Lift doors and reception desks, where everyone turns and stops.
  • Main walkways, where the shine wears away first.
  • Trolley routes, which leave scratches and chipped joints.
  • Entrances and balcony doors, where sand comes in.
Cleaning crews can also add to the problem. Strong cleaners can leave dull patches, and old wax builds up along the edges.
Restoration goes further than a polish, because it deals with damage first.

1. Inspect the floor and test any stains.
  2. Fill cracks and chips with a colour-matched filler.
  3. Grind uneven tile edges where the floor needs it.
  4. Hone out scratches and etching.
  5. Polish to the agreed finish and seal the stone.
Not every floor needs every step. A lightly worn apartment may only need honing and polishing, while a busy lobby may need grinding first. See how we approach marble floor restoration.
Most towers control when contractors can work, where they can park and which lifts they can use. Speak to your building manager early and ask about:

• Permitted working hours and noise limits.
  • Access to water and power.
  • Protection for lifts and shared corridors.
  • Any permit or insurance documents the building needs.
For offices and retail units, overnight or weekend work usually causes the least disruption. Share these details during the site visit so the plan fits your building.

You do not always need to close a whole floor. Teams can work in sections and keep a clear route open with barriers and signs. Wet floors can be slippery, so the area in use needs to stay marked until it dries.
In apartments, it helps to move small items out first and to agree which rooms the team will do on each day.
After restoration, a simple routine protects the floor.

• Use mats at lobby doors and lift entrances.
  • Dust-mop to remove sand before wet mopping.
  • Use pH-neutral cleaners only.
  • Clean up spills from coffee, juice and cleaning products quickly.
If your cleaning team is new to marble, ask them to read our guide on how often to polish marble floors.

Ripping out marble in a tower is expensive and disruptive. It means noise, debris and lift bookings, and it can damage the waterproofing beneath the floor. Restoration keeps the original stone and causes far less disruption.

Replacement starts to make sense only when tiles are loose, broken in large numbers, or badly water-damaged. Ask for an honest view of which tiles can be saved. In many cases, a few damaged tiles can be replaced and blended into the restored floor.

sections.h2: Common problems in Business Bay properties
body: Each type of space has its own pattern of damage.

• Apartments: sand from balconies, dull kitchens and water marks around bathrooms.
  • Offices: chair wheels, printer corners and coffee spills.
  • Lobbies: heavy traffic, cleaning machines and worn paths around reception desks.
  • Retail units: trolley marks and dull areas at the entrance.
Knowing the pattern helps us decide where to spend the most time, and where a lighter polish will do.

sections.h2: What affects the price and timing
body: The price depends on the area, the amount of damage, the access and the working hours. Night work, limited lift access and work in small sections can add time. Bring these details to the site visit, so that the quote reflects how the job will really run.
The time depends on the same things. We confirm a plan after the inspection, rather than guessing over the phone.

sections.h2: Questions to ask a restoration company
body:
• Can you show me a test area first?
  • How will you protect the lifts, walls and doors?
  • What happens to the water from the wet process?
  • How will you keep the area safe while people use it?
  • What can you not fix on this floor?
Clear answers are a good sign. If a company cannot explain its process, keep looking.
We reply within 30 minutes on call or WhatsApp, and we give you a visit time based on our schedule. The site inspection is free, and you get a fixed-price quote for the agreed work.

faqs.q: Can you restore marble in a lobby while the building stays open?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. We can work in sections and plan overnight or weekend work, depending on what your building allows.

faqs.q: Does restoration remove every mark?
faqs.a: It removes most wear and surface damage. Deep stains and old water damage may improve but not fully disappear. We tell you what to expect after we inspect the floor.

faqs.q: What do I need from my building manager?
faqs.a: Ask about working hours, lift access, water and power, and any permit the building needs. Share this with us before the work starts.

title: Onyx Care in Dubai Homes: Backlit Walls, Vanities and Floors
h1: Onyx in Dubai Homes: How to Care for Backlit Walls, Vanities and Floors
description: Onyx is beautiful but delicate. Learn how to clean it, what to avoid, and how to look after backlit walls, vanities and feature panels.
excerpt: Onyx is beautiful but delicate. Here is how to clean it and look after backlit walls, vanities and feature panels.
intro: Onyx glows like no other stone, and that is why people use it for backlit walls, reception counters and statement vanities. It is also softer and more fragile than marble, so ordinary cleaning habits can damage it. This guide explains how to look after onyx in daily use.

body: Onyx forms in thin bands, which is what lets light pass through it. Those bands also make it brittle. It scratches easily, reacts with acid, and can crack if it is knocked.
Many onyx slabs have a mesh or resin backing for support. That makes cleaning products and heat more important to think about, because they can affect the resin as well as the stone.
Keep it simple.

• Dust with a soft, dry cloth.
  • Wipe with a damp cloth and a pH-neutral stone cleaner.
  • Dry the surface straight away.
  • Use light pressure, as grit in a cloth can scratch the stone.
Do not use glass sprays on onyx walls, even if the surface looks like glass. Many of them contain ammonia or acid.

Bathrooms are hard on onyx. Water, soap and perfume all leave marks. Keep bottles on a tray, wipe the top dry and rinse off toothpaste quickly. A sealer helps slow stains, but it will not stop etching from acids.
Backlit onyx shows every mark, because light comes through from behind.

• Turn the lights off before cleaning, so you do not mistake reflections for dirt.
  • Check for dark patches, which can point to damp or old adhesive.
  • Check that the lights are not overheating the panel.
Replacing old lights with cooler LEDs can be a good idea, but ask an electrician first. If you see a new crack, stop cleaning and get it checked.

Onyx is rarely the best choice for busy floors, but you may have it in a feature area. Put mats near it, keep shoes with grit away where you can, and dust it often. Sand can damage onyx faster than marble.

A polisher can remove a cloudy haze, fine scratches and some water marks. The work needs fine abrasives, gentle pressure and a lot of hand work. Deep cracks or old damage may stay visible, so ask for an honest view first. See our onyx marble polishing service.

sections.h2: How to protect onyx during other work
body: Most onyx damage happens by accident. Painters, cleaners and electricians may not know how delicate it is.

• Cover the stone during any building work.
  • Tell your cleaners which surfaces are onyx.
  • Keep ladders and tools away from wall panels.
  • Keep tape off the surface, as some adhesives leave marks or lift the finish.
  • Check any new cleaning product on a hidden spot.
A short note for your cleaning team can save you an expensive repair.

Sealing can help slow stains on vanities and tops, but choose the product carefully. Some sealers change the look of the stone or reduce its glow. On backlit panels, test the sealer somewhere hidden first. Do not seal over a stain, because the mark will stay locked in.

Small chips and fissures can often be filled with clear or tinted resin. On a backlit panel, a repair can show when the light is on, so check it with the lights both on and off. If a panel has a large crack, the backing may have failed. In that case, have the fixing checked before any polishing starts.

sections.h2: Choosing onyx for a new space
body: If you are planning a renovation, think about how the room is used.

• Feature walls and ceilings are the safest places.
  • Vanity tops work if you are happy to wipe them dry and accept some marks.
  • Floors and busy counters are the highest risk.
Ask your installer how the panel will be fixed, and leave room for the lights to be reached. Good planning at the start makes future maintenance far easier.

• Using a glass spray on a backlit wall.
  • Scrubbing a haze with a rough sponge.
  • Leaving perfume bottles on a vanity.
  • Allowing lights to touch the back of the stone.
Call a specialist if you notice:

• Cracks that seem to be growing.
  • A loose or hollow-sounding panel.
  • Cloudy patches that do not clean off.
  • Uneven light across a wall.

faqs.q: Can onyx be used in a shower?
faqs.a: It can, but it needs careful sealing and regular care. Many owners prefer a tougher stone in wet areas.

faqs.q: How do I remove a white haze from onyx?
faqs.a: A haze usually comes from acid or water. Clean it gently first. If it stays, the surface needs professional polishing.

faqs.q: Is onyx harder to look after than marble?
faqs.a: Yes. It is softer and more brittle, so it needs gentle cleaning and careful handling.

title: Can Corian Be Repaired? Scratches, Burns and Dull Patches
h1: Can Corian Countertops Be Repaired? Scratches, Burns and Dull Patches
description: Corian is easier to repair than most surfaces. Learn what you can fix at home, what needs a professional, and how to choose a finish.
keywords: corian countertop polishing dubai abu dhabi
excerpt: Corian is easier to repair than most surfaces. Here is what you can fix at home and what needs a professional.
intro: Corian has one big advantage over stone: the colour runs all the way through it. That means many scratches, burns and stains can be sanded out instead of living with them for ever. Before you replace a worn top, find out what can be repaired and what it takes.

body: Corian is a solid surface made from acrylic resin and minerals. It is not stone, so you should not treat it like marble or granite. It does not need sealing, and it has no pores for stains to soak into. It is softer than stone, though, so it scratches more easily.

sections.h2: What you can fix at home
body: Light marks often come out with simple care.

• Use a non-abrasive cleaner and a damp cloth for everyday marks.
  • Rub in small circles, and clean the whole area so the finish stays even.
  • Rinse well and dry the surface.
Follow the maker's care guide if you have it. Rough pads can leave a patch that looks different from the rest of the top.
Some damage is best left to someone with the right tools.

• Deep scratches and knife marks.
  • Burns from hot pans.
  • Cracks near sinks and hobs.
  • Dull, patchy areas across a whole top.
  • Failed joints and seams.
A professional sands the area through finer and finer grits, and then finishes it to match the rest of the top. Our Corian countertop polishing service covers both repairs and full refinishing.

Heat is the main risk. A hot pan can leave a white or yellow mark, and sudden heat can crack the top near a hob. Always use a trivet. Do not rely on the top being heat-resistant just because it feels hard.
Corian can be refinished to matte, satin or gloss.

• Matte hides fine scratches best, and it is easy to touch up.
  • Satin suits most kitchens.
  • Gloss looks smart, but it shows every mark.
If your kitchen gets heavy use, a lower sheen will look better for longer.

Repair works well on most tops. Replacement may be better if large areas are cracked, if the top is badly stained from a leak underneath, or if a section has come away from its base. We can look at the top and advise you before you spend anything.
A full refinish treats the whole top, so the colour and sheen stay even.

1. The technician cleans the surface and checks the joints.
  2. Deep marks are sanded out first.
  3. The whole top is sanded through finer and finer grits.
  4. The final grit and pad set the sheen you have chosen.
  5. The edges and sink area are blended by hand.
The work creates fine dust, so the team protects the kitchen first. You should be able to use the top once the job is finished, but confirm this with the technician.
Knowing the weak spots helps you protect them.

• Around the hob, where heat can scorch or crack the top.
  • Near sinks, where stress and hot water can open joints.
  • Inner corners of cut-outs, where cracks start.
  • Dark colours, which show every fine scratch.
Check that hot appliances such as air fryers and slow cookers stand on a heat pad. Long heat from these machines can mark the surface as easily as a hot pan.

sections.h2: Corian or stone: which is easier to live with?
body: Corian is warmer to the touch and it hides joints well, and most damage can be repaired on site. Marble and granite resist heat better, but stone repairs are harder to hide. Neither is better for every home. If you have children or use your kitchen heavily, repairability may matter more to you than gloss.

• Using a sharp knife directly on the top.
  • Leaving nail varnish remover or paint stripper on it.
  • Using a green scourer on a gloss finish.
  • Pouring boiling water straight into a Corian sink without running cold water first.
These habits cause most of the repairs we see, and all of them are easy to change.

• Clean with mild soap and water.
  • Use chopping boards and trivets.
  • Wipe up dyes and strong chemicals quickly.
  • Avoid harsh solvents.

faqs.q: Can burns be removed from Corian?
faqs.a: Most surface burns can be sanded out. A deep burn may need a section to be cut out and replaced.

faqs.q: Does Corian need sealing?
faqs.a: No. It has no pores, so sealers are not needed.

faqs.q: Will a repair show?
faqs.a: A good repair blends in. A matte or satin finish hides repairs best. High gloss makes small differences easier to see.

title: Can Quartz Be Polished? What Works and What Does Not
h1: Can Quartz Be Polished? What Works and What Does Not
description: Quartz cannot be polished the way marble can. Learn which quartz marks can be improved, which cannot, and how to protect your top.
keywords: quartz polishing dubai dubai united arab emirates
excerpt: Quartz cannot be polished the way marble can. Here is which marks can be improved and which cannot.
intro: If your quartz top has lost its shine, you may wonder whether it can be polished like marble. The honest answer is: partly. Quartz is made differently from natural stone, so some damage can be improved and some cannot. Here is what to expect before you spend money.

body: Engineered quartz is mostly crushed quartz mixed with resin and pigment. The factory presses it into slabs and polishes it under controlled conditions. That gives you a hard, non-porous surface that resists stains and does not need sealing.
The resin is the weak point. Heat, strong chemicals and strong sunlight can all affect it.

sections.h2: Check whether it is really dull
body: Many quartz tops only look dull because of residue from cleaning sprays or cooking oil. Try this first.

1. Wash the area with warm water and mild dish soap.
  2. Rinse with clean water.
  3. Dry it with a soft cloth.
  4. Look at it again in the light.
If the shine returns, you only need to change your cleaning products.
A specialist can often improve:

• Light scratches from pans and cutlery.
  • Dull patches from cleaning products.
  • Stubborn marks on the surface.
This work needs low speed and low heat. Too much heat can damage the resin, and that can leave a mark worse than the one you started with.
Be realistic about these.

• Burn marks from hot pans often stay, because they are in the resin.
  • Colour changes caused by bleach or sunlight are hard to reverse.
  • Deep chips need a filler, and the repair may show.
If someone promises to make burnt quartz look brand new, ask them how they will do it.

sections.h2: Do not treat quartz like marble
body: Marble products can harm quartz. Avoid crystallization products, and do not use acidic stone polishes or wax. Quartz does not need sealing in the normal way. An optional protective product may help keep oil off a worn surface, but it is not essential on a healthy top.

• Use trivets for hot pans.
  • Clean with mild soap and water.
  • Avoid bleach, oven cleaner and paint stripper.
  • Use chopping boards.
  • Keep outdoor tops out of strong sun where you can.

sections.h2: Common quartz problems, and what causes them
body:
• Pale or yellow patches near the hob usually come from heat.
  • Dull rings often come from cleaners or from hot, wet pots.
  • Faded areas near windows can come from strong sunlight.
  • A sticky feel usually comes from product residue.
  • Dark marks on a light top can be metal rubbing off a pan.
Metal marks look like scratches, but they often lift with a soft cloth and a mild cream cleaner. Test it in a hidden corner first.

Mild dish soap and warm water are enough for daily cleaning. For dried food, use a plastic scraper. Glass cleaners may be fine for occasional use, but they can leave a film, so rinse afterwards. Avoid bleach, oven cleaner, paint stripper and drain cleaner, as they can attack the resin.

sections.h2: Quartz outdoors and in sunny kitchens
body: Most quartz is made for indoor use. Strong sun can fade the colour over time, particularly on darker tops. If your top sits under a big window, a blind helps during the hottest hours. Outdoor kitchens need a material made for that use, so check with your supplier first.

A repair is worth trying when the damage is small or in one area. Replacement may be better if a burn sits in the middle of a top, if the top has cracked right through, or if a large area has faded. A local repair may still show, so ask to see a sample if you can.

• Putting a pan straight on the top because quartz "can take it".
  • Using a slow cooker or air fryer without a heat pad.
  • Applying marble polish or wax.
  • Using a rough scourer on dried food.
Send us a photo on WhatsApp, and we reply within 30 minutes. We can tell you whether a quartz polishing visit is worth it, or whether a better clean will do the job.

faqs.q: Can quartz be restored to a factory shine?
faqs.a: Often it can be improved, but not always matched exactly. It depends on the damage and how worn the surface is.

faqs.q: Does quartz need sealing?
faqs.a: No. It is not porous like natural stone, so normal sealing is not needed.

faqs.q: Why does my quartz look cloudy?
faqs.a: It is usually residue from a cleaner or oil. Wash it with mild soap and water first.

title: Does Granite Need Polishing? Signs, Sealing and Care
h1: Does Granite Need Polishing? Signs, Sealing and Daily Care
description: Granite is hard, but it can still lose its shine. Learn when granite needs polishing, when it only needs sealing, and how to care for it.
excerpt: Granite is hard, but it can still lose its shine. Here is when it needs polishing, when it needs sealing and how to care for it.
intro: Granite has a reputation for being almost indestructible, and it is much tougher than marble. It can still lose its shine, though, and many owners do not know whether their stone needs polishing, sealing or simply a better clean. This guide helps you work out which one applies.

body: Granite resists most kitchen acids and scratches, but it still wears.

• Heavy foot traffic slowly dulls floors, especially at entrances.
  • Grit under chairs and pans wears down busy areas.
  • Greasy residue and harsh cleaners leave a film that looks like dullness.
  • Old coatings wear unevenly and leave patches.
Many dull granite tops are simply dirty. Wash the surface with warm water and a little mild soap, then dry it with a soft cloth. If the shine comes back, you only need a better routine.
If it still looks flat, or if you can see a worn area in the light, the surface itself has worn down.
Not all granite needs the same protection. Some dense stones absorb very little, while lighter stones can soak up oil and water. A simple test tells you.

1. Put a few drops of water on the stone.
  2. Leave them for around ten minutes.
  3. Wipe the area dry.
  4. If the stone has turned darker, it is absorbing water and needs sealing.
Sealing helps against stains, but it does not add shine.
Polishing makes sense when you can see:

• Dull paths on a floor.
  • Worn areas on a kitchen top.
  • Light scratches that do not wipe off.
  • Patchy shine from old coatings.

Granite is very hard, so it needs heavy machines and diamond pads. Crystallization products made for marble will not work on it. Be careful with any quick polish that relies on wax. It may look good for a while, but it will wear away. See how our granite polishing service works.

Chips on edges are common around sinks and on stair treads. A colour-matched filler can make them much less visible. Cracks need checking first, in case the stone is moving because of the base beneath it.

Many dark or speckled stones are sold as granite, but some are closer to other stone types. It matters, because the right care depends on the stone. Lemon juice is a simple clue. Put a drop on a hidden corner and wipe it off after a minute. If it leaves a dull mark, you may have a calcium-based stone, not true granite.
Some black stones are also dyed or waxed at the factory to look darker. If colour comes off on a cloth when you use a solvent, ask a stone specialist to look at it before you treat it.

Granite floors in villas and lobbies wear slowly, but they show dull paths in time. Sand scratches the polish, and heavy cleaning can leave a film. Stair treads need extra care, because the front edge takes the most wear and a high polish can be slippery. Ask for a finish that suits how you use the stairs.
Granite is a strong kitchen surface, but it has some weak points.

• Oil can darken lighter stones if the seal has worn away.
  • Edges around the sink can chip.
  • Knife blades can dull quickly on the hard surface.
  • Very hot pans can stress the stone, especially near a joint.
A quick wipe with warm soapy water after cooking prevents most problems. Avoid glass cleaners, which can leave a film.

• Sealing a dense granite that does not need it. The sealer stays on the surface and leaves a haze.
  • Using oil or wax to make the stone look darker. It wears off unevenly.
  • Using vinegar every day. Granite resists acid, but it can harm the sealer.
  • Using a rough pad on a polished top.
If your granite looks hazy after a recent seal, a stone company can remove the excess.

• Clean with warm water and mild soap.
  • Avoid bleach, ammonia and rough pads.
  • Wipe up oil and wine, even though granite resists stains well.
  • Use trivets for very hot pans, because sudden heat can stress the stone.
  • Use mats at doors to keep grit away from floors.

faqs.q: Is granite polishing the same as marble polishing?
faqs.a: The idea is the same, but granite is much harder. It needs heavier machines and different pads, and crystallization does not work on it.

faqs.q: Can dull granite be restored without replacing it?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Diamond polishing can bring back the shine on floors and tops.

faqs.q: How often does granite need sealing?
faqs.a: It depends on the stone and how much you use it. Use the water test. If the stone darkens, seal it.

title: Old Terrazzo Floors: Restore or Replace?
h1: Old Terrazzo Floors: Should You Restore or Replace Them?
description: Old terrazzo can often be restored for less than the cost of replacing it. Learn how to judge your floor and what restoration involves.
excerpt: Old terrazzo can often be restored. Here is how to judge your floor and what restoration involves.
intro: Many older UAE buildings still have their original terrazzo floors, often hidden under wax, tiles or carpet. Owners often assume they need to rip them out, but terrazzo is one of the most repairable floors you can have. Here is how to decide whether yours is worth saving.

body: Terrazzo is made from chips of marble, granite or glass set in cement or epoxy. The mix is ground flat and polished. Because the chips run through the whole thickness of the floor, grinding reveals fresh surface rather than wearing it away.
That is why old terrazzo can look so good again.

sections.h2: Signs your floor can be restored
body: Most floors are worth restoring if:

• The floor is solid and does not sound hollow.
  • The cracks are few and small.
  • The chips are still firmly in place.
  • The damage is mostly dullness, stains or old wax.
Think harder if you see:

• Large areas that sound hollow when tapped.
  • Wide cracks that keep moving.
  • Water damage from below.
  • Big missing sections that would be hard to match.
Even then, restoring part of the floor may cost less than replacing all of it. The base beneath the floor is what matters most.

1. Remove old wax, glue or coatings.
  2. Repair cracks and holes with a matching filler.
  3. Grind the surface flat with diamond tools.
  4. Polish through finer grits.
  5. Seal the floor to protect it.
Grinding is wet, which keeps dust down, but it is still a big job. Plan for it as you would for other home repairs. See our terrazzo polishing service.

Old terrazzo has character, and small differences in repairs are normal. New filler can be matched closely, but it may not be perfect. Most owners find that this adds to the charm of an older floor. If you need a perfect match, talk about it before the work starts.
Removing tiles can reveal terrazzo in good condition, but the adhesive can leave marks. Lift a small area first if you can. Our team can then tell you how much work the floor would need.

Restoration prices depend on the area, the condition and the finish. When you compare it with replacement, count the removal, disposal, new floor and any change in door heights. We inspect the floor for free and give you a fixed price for the agreed work.

sections.h2: How to test a terrazzo floor
body: A few simple checks tell you a lot.

1. Tap the floor with a broom handle or a coin. A dull, hollow sound can mean that it has come loose from its base.
  2. Look along the cracks. Fine hairline cracks are common, but wide ones need attention.
  3. Look for loose chips, especially at joints and edges.
  4. Scratch a hidden corner gently. If a yellow film comes off, the floor has been waxed.
  5. Wet a small area. It will show you the colours you can expect after polishing.
That last test is a good way to see the floor's potential before you decide.

Most older UAE floors use cement. It is hard-wearing, but it is porous and it can stain, so sealing helps. Newer commercial floors may use epoxy, which is less porous but can be marked by heat and chemicals. The two types need different care, so identify yours before you buy any products.
Terrazzo can take a high shine, but it also looks good with a softer finish.

• High gloss suits lobbies and formal rooms.
  • Satin hides wear better in family homes.
  • A slip-resistant finish suits wet areas and ramps.
Choose based on how you use the space, not only how the floor looks in a photo.
Grinding uses heavy machines and water, so plan ahead.

• Clear the room, and protect any doors and built-in furniture.
  • Tell the team if there are hidden pipes or cables in the floor.
  • Think about skirting boards, which may need a touch-up afterwards.
  • Allow time for the floor to dry before you seal it or move back in.
Older buildings can have thin floors in places, so a good company will check this before grinding.

• Sweep regularly to remove sand.
  • Clean with a pH-neutral cleaner.
  • Avoid acid cleaners, which can eat into the marble chips.
  • Reseal when water starts to soak in.

faqs.q: Can you remove old wax from terrazzo?
faqs.a: Yes. Stripping the wax is often the first step, and many floors look much better straight away.

faqs.q: Is restored terrazzo slippery?
faqs.a: It can be slippery when wet, like any smooth floor. We can discuss the finish that suits the area.

faqs.q: Can cracks in terrazzo be repaired?
faqs.a: Yes. We fill small cracks with a matching filler. Moving cracks need a check of the base first.

title: Marble Polishing in Dubai: What to Know Before You Book
h1: Marble Polishing in Dubai: What to Know Before You Book
description: What to check before you book marble polishing in Dubai: what the job involves, what a fair quote covers, and the questions to ask any company.
keywords: marble polishing guide dubai, marble care dubai
excerpt: Before you book marble polishing in Dubai, learn what the job involves, what a quote should cover and which questions to ask.
intro: Booking marble polishing for the first time can feel confusing. Companies use different words, quotes look different, and it is hard to tell a real polish from a quick shine. This guide explains what happens during the job, what to ask before you agree, and how to get ready for the work.

body: Marble shines because its surface is smooth. Sand, shoes and cleaning products slowly scratch that surface, so light scatters and the floor looks dull. Real polishing removes a very thin layer of worn stone with diamond pads, working from coarse grits to fine ones.
A wax or a shine spray is different. It adds a layer on top of the stone, and that layer wears off. If a company promises a fast shine with no machine work, ask what product they use.
These words describe different steps, and you may not need all of them.

• Honing smooths the stone and leaves a soft, satin finish.
  • Polishing takes the same surface up to a high shine.
  • Crystallization treats the top of the stone to harden it and add gloss.
  • Sealing helps keep spills out of the stone.
Our guide to polishing and crystallization explains how the last two steps differ.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you book
body: A good company should answer these clearly.

• Will you inspect the floor before you give a price?
  • Which grits and products will you use on my stone?
  • What is included: edges, corners, skirting, sealing?
  • How will you protect my furniture, walls and doors?
  • Will the price change after you start?
  • What can polishing not fix on this floor?
The last question matters most. Deep cracks, old water damage and some stains need extra work, and an honest company will tell you that before the job starts.

sections.h2: How to get your home ready
body: A little preparation makes the job faster and safer.

• Move small items, rugs and anything fragile.
  • Tell the team about any loose tiles or recent repairs.
  • Check building rules on working hours if you live in a tower.
  • Plan to keep off the floor for a while after the final seal.
The crew will usually move and cover larger furniture with you, but it helps to agree this first.

sections.h2: What to do after the polish
body: Sand is the biggest enemy of a polished floor in Dubai. Put mats at every door and dust-mop often. Clean with a pH-neutral stone cleaner, and wipe up lemon, vinegar and juice straight away. Our guide on how to care for marble floors gives you a simple routine.

sections.h2: What affects the price of marble polishing
body: Fair companies inspect the floor before they quote, because two floors of the same size can need very different work. These are the main things that move the price.

• The area, and how many rooms, stairs and edges it includes.
  • The type of stone, as soft or delicate stones need slower work.
  • The condition of the floor, including scratches, etching and stains.
  • Repairs such as filling cracks or grinding raised tile edges.
  • The finish you want, and whether you want crystallization or sealing.
  • Access, such as tower rules or night work.
Compare quotes by scope, not only by the final number. A low price often leaves out edges, stairs or sealing. Our marble polishing cost guide explains this in more detail.

Time depends on the size of the area and the condition of the stone. A lightly worn room moves faster than a floor that needs grinding and repairs. Stairs and edges take longer, because much of the work happens by hand.
Ask for a realistic plan after the inspection, not a promise over the phone. If you live at home during the work, ask which rooms the team will do each day, so that you can plan around them.

• Polishing before fixing a leak. Damp stone will mark again.
  • Choosing a shine product instead of real polishing. It wears off and can make future work harder.
  • Mopping with vinegar or a strong floor cleaner after the job. Acid removes the shine you just paid for.
  • Walking on the floor too soon after sealing. Ask how long to wait.
  • Polishing a single patch. It can leave a visible difference, so ask whether you should do the whole room.

sections.h2: How to tell if the job went well
body: Check the floor in daylight, from a low angle. Look for even shine from wall to wall, clean corners and skirting, and no swirl marks. Ask the team to walk through it with you before they leave, and raise anything you are not happy with straight away.

If you want your floor checked, see our marble polishing service in Dubai. The inspection is free, and we reply within 30 minutes on call or WhatsApp. We then give you a visit time based on our schedule.

faqs.q: How do I know if my floor needs polishing or just cleaning?
faqs.a: Clean a small dull area with a pH-neutral cleaner and let it dry. If it still looks dull or you can see scratches in the light, the surface is worn, and cleaning will not fix it.

faqs.q: Can you polish a floor while we live at home?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Teams usually work room by room and use a wet process, which keeps dust down. You will need to stay off wet areas until they are ready.

faqs.q: Does every marble floor need crystallization?
faqs.a: No. It suits calcium-based stone that needs a harder, glossier surface. Some homes prefer a honed look or only need sealing.

title: How to Care for Calacatta Marble in a Dubai Home
h1: How to Care for Calacatta Marble in a Dubai Home
description: A practical guide to caring for Calacatta marble: daily cleaning, what to avoid, how to handle spills, and when to call a professional.
excerpt: Daily cleaning, what to avoid and when to call a professional: a simple care guide for Calacatta marble in Dubai homes.
intro: Calacatta is one of the most striking marbles you can put in a home, but its white surface shows everything. A lemon wedge on the counter or a splash of cleaner can leave a mark in minutes. The good news is that a simple routine prevents most problems. Here is how to look after it.

body: Calacatta is a calcium-based stone, so acids react with it. It is also porous, which means coffee, oil and wine can soak in. On a white background, marks that would hide on a darker stone stand out at once.
White marble can also yellow over time, especially where water sits on the stone or gets underneath it.
A short routine does most of the work.

• Dust-mop floors daily to remove sand.
  • Wipe tops with a soft cloth and warm water.
  • Use a pH-neutral stone cleaner once a week.
  • Dry bathroom surfaces after use, so that water does not sit.
Avoid microfibre cloths with grit in them, and rinse them often.

sections.h2: What to keep away from Calacatta
body: These common products can mark the stone.

• Vinegar, lemon and other acidic cleaners.
  • Bleach and bathroom sprays.
  • Scouring powders and rough pads.
  • Perfume and some cosmetics, on vanity tops.
Put trays under perfume bottles and soap dispensers. In the kitchen, use coasters and chopping boards.

Speed matters most. Blot the spill with a soft cloth instead of wiping it across the stone. Rinse with water and dry the area. If a mark stays, do not scrub it. Scrubbing can make a dull patch bigger.

Stains and etch marks need different treatment. A stain looks darker than the stone, because something has soaked in. An etch mark looks dull or pale, because acid has damaged the surface. Our guide to etch marks explains how to tell them apart.
Some problems are beyond home care.

• Dull rings that will not clean off.
  • Yellow patches that keep spreading.
  • Water that soaks in instead of beading on the surface.
  • Scratches you can feel with a fingernail.
For these, see our Calacatta marble polishing service. Polishing removes surface damage, and sealing gives you more time to deal with spills.
Calacatta is used across the home, and each room has its own risks.
Kitchens
Keep lemons, vinegar and wine away from the stone. Use boards and trays, and check the sink area often, because water sits there.
Bathrooms
Soap, perfume and hair products are the main risks. Keep them on trays, and wipe the vanity dry. Squeegee shower walls after use.
Floors
Sand is the biggest issue. Use mats at the entrance and dust-mop every day. Add felt pads to chair legs.
Stairs and walls
Stairs wear on the front edge. Walls usually need only gentle dusting, but check them for splashes from cleaning products.

Read the label before you buy any cleaner. Avoid anything that lists acid, bleach or ammonia. A product that says it is safe for stone is a better start, but check that it says pH-neutral. Coloured cleaning liquids and dyed soaps can also leave a tint on white marble, so a clear product is the safer choice.
Avoid oil soaps and wax-based shine products. They leave a film that attracts dirt and can turn yellow.

• Leaving a wet cloth or sponge on the stone.
  • Putting rubber-backed mats on the floor, which can stain or trap moisture.
  • Using a steam mop, which pushes heat and water into the stone.
  • Scrubbing a mark with a rough pad.
  • Using a floor polish from a supermarket.

sections.h2: What to expect as the stone ages
body: Natural marble changes with use. Light etching on a kitchen top is normal, and some owners like the look of a stone that shows its age. If you want it to stay bright, plan for professional polishing from time to time. A polish removes the wear, and a fresh seal helps with spills. Our guide to how often to polish marble can help you plan.
If you are renovating, think about how you use the space. A polished finish looks bright but shows etch marks. A honed finish looks softer and hides light marks better, which can suit a busy kitchen.

faqs.q: Is Calacatta a good choice for a kitchen?
faqs.a: It can be, if you accept some marks over time. Sealing and quick clean-up help, but acid can still etch it.

faqs.q: Why is my white marble turning yellow?
faqs.a: Common causes include water, old wax and iron minerals in the stone. Read our guide on why white marble turns yellow.

faqs.q: How often should Calacatta be sealed?
faqs.a: It depends on use. Test it with a few drops of water. If the stone darkens within a few minutes, it is time to reseal.

title: Travertine Floors: Filled or Unfilled, Honed or Polished?
h1: Travertine Floors: Filled or Unfilled, Honed or Polished?
description: Choosing or restoring travertine? Compare filled and unfilled stone, and honed and polished finishes, so you get the right look for your home.
excerpt: Compare filled and unfilled travertine, and honed and polished finishes, so you get the right look for your home.
intro: Travertine has a warm, natural look that suits UAE villas, but it comes in several types and finishes. These choices affect how it looks, how it feels and how much care it needs. Whether you are choosing new stone or restoring an old floor, here is what the words mean.

body: Travertine is a form of limestone that builds up around mineral springs. Gas and water leave small holes as the stone forms. These holes give it its character, but they also collect dirt if nobody fills them.

• Filled travertine has its holes filled at the factory, usually with resin or cement. The surface is smooth and easy to clean.
  • Unfilled travertine keeps its natural holes. It looks more rustic, but dirt settles in them.
Indoors, most owners prefer filled stone. If your filler has worn away, it can be replaced with a colour-matched filler.

FinishLookBest for
PolishedShiny and formalHalls and low-traffic rooms
HonedSoft and satinMost floors in the home
BrushedTextured and naturalTerraces and rustic rooms
TumbledAged, rounded edgesOutdoor and feature areas

Honed is usually the safest choice for floors. It hides scratches and etch marks better, and it has more grip than a high polish. Polished travertine looks striking, but it shows wear in busy rooms. Outdoors, choose a textured finish, as smooth stone can be slippery when wet.
Old floors often have worn filler and dark, dirty holes. Polishing alone will not fix that. The usual order is:

1. Deep clean the stone.
  2. Fill the holes with a colour-matched filler.
  3. Hone the floor to level the filler and the stone.
  4. Polish, if you want more shine.
  5. Seal the stone.
Our travertine polishing service follows these steps.
Yes. A polished floor can be honed to a softer look, and a honed floor can be polished to more shine. The stone and its condition limit how far you can go, so check this during an inspection.

sections.h2: How to tell what you have
body: Look closely at your floor.

• If you can see small pits and dirt in them, it is unfilled or the filler has worn out.
  • If the holes look smooth and slightly darker, they are probably filled.
  • If the surface reflects clearly, it is polished.
  • If it looks soft with little reflection, it is honed.
  • If the edges look rounded and worn, it is tumbled.
Knowing this helps you to ask for the right work, and it stops you paying for a finish that will not last.

Travertine is porous, so sealing matters. An impregnating sealer soaks in and slows down spills, without changing the look much. Avoid thick topical coatings, especially outdoors. They can trap moisture, peel and turn cloudy.
Clean the stone well first. If you seal over dirt in the holes, the dirt stays there.

Terraces and pool areas take sun, salt and water. Choose a textured finish for better grip, and use a sealer made for outdoor stone. Rinse chlorine and salt off the surface, and clean any green growth with a product that is safe for limestone. Pressure washers can damage soft stone, so keep the pressure low.

Travertine looks good in bathrooms, but soap film builds up in the holes. Choose filled stone, keep it sealed and use a pH-neutral cleaner. Squeegee the walls after a shower. Acid-based limescale removers will etch the stone, so keep them away from it.

• Polishing a floor without filling the holes.
  • Using vinegar to clean soap film.
  • Mopping dirt into the holes with dirty water.
  • Using a topical sealer on outdoor stone.
  • Filling holes with a colour that does not match, as this can stand out.
Ask to see a filler sample on your stone before the work starts.

• Vacuum or sweep often, as grit collects in the holes.
  • Use a pH-neutral cleaner.
  • Avoid vinegar and lemon, which damage limestone.
  • Reseal when water starts to soak in.

faqs.q: Is travertine stronger than marble?
faqs.a: It is usually softer and more porous, so it needs good sealing and gentle cleaning.

faqs.q: Can I fill the holes myself?
faqs.a: Small repairs are possible, but a large floor needs matched filler and honing to look even.

faqs.q: Is travertine good around a pool?
faqs.a: Yes, in a textured finish. Keep it sealed and rinse off chlorine and salt.

title: Crystallization or Sealing: Which Protects Marble Better?
h1: Crystallization or Sealing: Which Protects Your Marble Better?
description: Crystallization and sealing protect marble in different ways. Learn how each one works, what it cannot do, and which suits your floor.
keywords: marble crystallization sealing dubai business bay
excerpt: Crystallization and sealing protect marble in different ways. Here is how to choose the right one for your floor.
intro: People often treat crystallization and sealing as the same thing, but they do different jobs. One works on the surface of the stone, and the other works inside its pores. Knowing the difference helps you pay for the protection your floor actually needs.

body: Crystallization uses a chemical treatment and a floor machine to change the top of the stone. The product reacts with the calcium in marble and forms a harder, glossier surface. It suits floors that need more shine and that take regular foot traffic.
It only works on calcium-based stone, such as marble, limestone and terrazzo with marble chips. It will not work on granite or quartz.

An impregnating sealer soaks into the stone and fills its tiny pores. It does not add much shine, and you often cannot see it at all. Its job is to slow down water, oil and other spills so that you have time to wipe them up.
Sealing suits kitchens, bathrooms and dining areas, where stains are the main risk.

CrystallizationSealing
Works on the surfaceWorks inside the pores
Adds hardness and glossSlows stains
Suits calcium-based stoneSuits most natural stone
Best on floorsBest on floors, tops and wet areas
No treatment makes marble maintenance-free.

• Acid can still mark the surface, so wipe up lemon and vinegar quickly.
  • Sand can still scratch the floor, so you still need mats and dust-mopping.
  • Neither one fixes deep scratches. The floor must be polished first.
Be careful with any company that promises a floor that never stains or never needs care.
Think about what worries you most.

• If your floor looks dull and sees heavy use, crystallization may help after polishing.
  • If you worry about stains in a kitchen or bathroom, choose a sealer.
  • If you have a busy floor that also faces spills, you may need both.
  • If you have granite, quartz or Corian, skip crystallization and ask about the right care for that surface.

sections.h2: In what order should the work happen?
body: Polish first, because both treatments protect the surface they find. Crystallizing or sealing a scratched floor only locks in the problem. Our crystallization and sealing service starts with a check of your stone, so you only pay for what the floor needs.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you pay for either
body: Protection products vary, so ask what you are getting.

• Which product will you use, and is it made for my stone?
  • Will you polish the floor first?
  • Will you test a small area?
  • How should I clean the floor afterwards?
  • What will the finish look like?
A company that only offers one answer for every floor may be selling a product rather than solving your problem.

sections.h2: Where each treatment works best in a home
body: Different rooms have different needs.

• Hallways and living rooms: traffic is the main issue, so polishing and possibly crystallization make sense.
  • Kitchens: oil and food stains matter most, so a good sealer is the priority.
  • Bathrooms: water and soap are the main issues, so use a sealer made for wet areas.
  • Stairs: wear shows on the front edge, and shiny treads can be slippery, so take care with the finish.
  • Outdoor stone: choose a breathable sealer, and avoid a high gloss.

• Sealing a floor that is still damp. It can trap moisture in the stone.
  • Sealing over old wax. The product cannot reach the stone.
  • Applying too much sealer. It can leave a sticky or streaky film.
  • Using crystallization on the wrong stone. It may not work, and it can leave marks.
  • Using acidic cleaners afterwards. They wear away the finish.

Protection lasts longer if you clean the right way. Dust-mop daily, use a pH-neutral cleaner and keep mats at the doors. A cleaning machine with a harsh pad can remove crystallization quickly, so tell your cleaning team what was done. Our guide on how often to polish marble floors can help you plan the next visit.

sections.h2: How do you know when to redo it?
body: Pour a little water on the stone and leave it for a few minutes. If the stone turns dark, the sealer has worn thin. For crystallization, look for dull paths where people walk most. Traffic and cleaning products decide how long each treatment lasts, so there is no fixed date.

faqs.q: Does crystallization make marble slippery?
faqs.a: It adds shine, but the surface is not necessarily more slippery when dry. Any polished stone can be slippery when wet, so keep floors dry and use mats near water.

faqs.q: Can I seal marble myself?
faqs.a: You can, but clean the stone well and follow the product label. Sealing over stains or dirt can trap them in the stone.

faqs.q: Can you crystallize granite?
faqs.a: No. Crystallization needs calcium in the stone, and granite does not have enough of it. Granite is polished with diamond pads instead.

title: Which Kitchen Tops Can Be Polished? Marble, Granite and More
h1: Which Kitchen Tops Can Be Polished? Marble, Granite, Quartz and Corian Compared
description: Marble, granite, quartz and Corian kitchen tops all respond differently to polishing. Compare what each one can and cannot do.
excerpt: Marble, granite, quartz and Corian all respond differently to polishing. Here is what each one can and cannot do.
intro: A dull kitchen top does not always need replacing. Whether you can restore it depends on what it is made of, because each material reacts differently to polishing, heat and chemicals. Use this guide to work out what you have and what is possible.

sections.h2: How to identify your kitchen top
body: If you do not have the paperwork, these clues can help.

• Marble has soft veins and marks easily with lemon.
  • Granite has speckles and feels very hard.
  • Quartz has an even pattern and a slightly plastic feel when it is tapped.
  • Corian feels warmer, and its joints are almost invisible.
If you are still unsure, send a photo. We can confirm the material at a free inspection.

MaterialCan it be polished?Main riskNeeds sealing?
MarbleYes, very wellAcid and stainsYes
GraniteYes, with heavy machinesChips on edgesSometimes
QuartzPartlyHeat and strong chemicalsNo
CorianYes, by sandingHeat and scratchesNo

Marble gives the best result from polishing, but it also needs it most. Acids from food leave dull marks. A polish removes them, and a sealer slows down stains. It does not stop acid, so spills still need quick attention. Our marble countertop service explains more.
Granite resists most food acids, so it often only needs a deep clean and a new seal. If it has worn near the sink or the hob, diamond polishing can bring the shine back.

Quartz comes from the factory with a polish that is hard to match on site. A specialist can often reduce light scratches and dull patches, but heat marks in the resin may stay. Be wary of anyone who promises to make burnt quartz look new.
Corian is the easiest to repair. Scratches and many burns can be sanded out, and the whole top can be refinished to a new sheen. It does not need a sealer.

sections.h2: Getting the job done with the least disruption
body: You do not need to remove the top or the sink. The team protects your cabinets, works in place and tells you when you can use the kitchen again. See how kitchen top polishing works. The time needed depends on the material, the size of the top and the damage, so we confirm this after the inspection.

sections.h2: How to judge the damage on your top
body: Before you call anyone, look at your top in good light.

• Wipe it clean, then look along the surface from a low angle.
  • Run a fingernail over any scratch. If it catches, the mark is deep.
  • Look at the area around the sink and the hob, where wear starts.
  • Put a few drops of water on natural stone, and see whether it soaks in.
  • Check joints and edges for gaps or chips.
Take a few photos. These help a technician give you useful advice, even before a site visit.
Most kitchen tops do not need replacing. Think about it in three steps.

• A repair fixes one chip, scratch or stain.
  • A refinish restores the whole surface, so it looks even.
  • A replacement makes sense only if the top is cracked through, badly burnt across a large area, or being changed for a new kitchen layout.
Replacement can also mean new plumbing, tiling and cabinet work, so count that cost too.
A high gloss looks smart, but it shows marks. If you cook every day, a satin or honed finish on marble or Corian can look better for longer. Granite and quartz usually keep their polished finish.

sections.h2: Mistakes that shorten the life of any top
body:
• Using one spray cleaner for every surface.
  • Standing on the top to reach a cupboard. It can crack near sink cut-outs.
  • Leaving a wet sponge or cloth on the surface.
  • Using the top as a chopping board.
  • Putting a hot pan down "just for a minute".
Keep a mild soap and a soft cloth near the sink, and you avoid most of these problems.

sections.h2: Simple habits that protect any top
body:
• Use chopping boards and trivets.
  • Wipe up spills quickly.
  • Avoid scouring pads and bleach.
  • Clean with mild soap or a product made for that material.

faqs.q: Can you polish a kitchen top without removing it?
faqs.a: Yes. We work in place and protect the cabinets, sink and walls around it.

faqs.q: Which kitchen top is easiest to repair?
faqs.a: Corian is usually the easiest, because scratches and many burns can be sanded out.

faqs.q: Can burnt quartz be fixed?
faqs.a: Sometimes it can be reduced, but a burn in the resin may not fully disappear. We check it first and tell you what to expect.

title: Why White Marble Turns Yellow in Dubai Homes
h1: Why White Marble Turns Yellow in Dubai Homes
description: White marble can turn yellow for several reasons. Learn the common causes, how to spot each one and which treatments work.
keywords: yellow stain removing marble dubai company
excerpt: White marble can turn yellow for several reasons. Here is how to spot the cause and which treatments work.
intro: White marble looks clean and bright when it is new, so a yellow patch is hard to ignore. Many owners try bleach or strong cleaners, which often make the problem worse. The right fix depends on what caused the colour, so start by working out the source.

body: Wax and some topical sealers yellow with age. The colour usually sits on the surface and looks uneven, and it can feel sticky. A stone-safe stripper may lift it. This is the easiest cause to fix.

Some white marbles contain tiny iron minerals. When water reaches them, they can oxidise and turn yellow or brown, a little like rust. This often appears after a lot of wet mopping or a poor wet polish.

If the yellow appears near showers, kitchens or along joints, water may be moving through the stone. It can bring minerals up from the mortar under the tile. Fix the leak first. Otherwise, the stain will come back.
Bleach, rust from metal cans, and dyes from mats can all leave marks. Rust marks tend to have a clear shape. Bleach can damage the surface as well as change its colour.
Ask yourself these questions.

• Is the colour even, or is it worse in walkways? This may point to wax or wear.
  • Is it near water? This may point to a leak or a damp floor.
  • Does it have a clear shape? This may point to something that stood on the floor.
  • Did it appear after cleaning or polishing? This may point to water reaching iron in the stone.

• Surface yellowing: strip the old coating, then polish.
  • Deep yellowing: use a poultice or a specialist stain treatment, often more than once.
  • Water-related yellowing: fix the source, let the floor dry, and then treat the stain.
Results depend on how deep the colour goes. Some stains go completely, and others only fade. We test a small area first, so you can see what to expect. See our yellow stain removal service.

• Do not use bleach. It rarely fixes the colour, and it can damage the surface.
  • Do not use acid cleaners. They will etch the marble.
  • Do not soak the floor. More water can make the problem worse.
  • Do not seal over a stain. It will trap the colour.
Some problems look like yellowing but are not.

• Dirt in the grout can make a whole floor look yellow. Clean a small area first.
  • Warm lighting can make white marble look cream. Check it in daylight.
  • A cream or beige stone may just be its natural colour. Compare it with a piece from a clean, hidden area.
  • Sealers can darken stone slightly. Compare sealed and unsealed areas if you can.
These checks take a few minutes, and they could save you the cost of a treatment you do not need.

A poultice is a paste that sits on the stain and slowly draws the colour out as it dries. It usually stays in place for a day or more under a cover. Different stains need different chemicals, which is why the cause matters so much. A deep stain may need several rounds, and the area may need polishing afterwards to match the rest of the floor.
The location often gives you the answer.

• Near showers and basins: water moving through the stone.
  • In one room after a renovation: mortar, adhesive or moisture.
  • Under plants: water and iron from the pot.
  • Under mats: rubber backing or trapped damp.
  • Across the whole floor: old wax or a cleaning product.
Take a photo of the whole room as well as a close-up of the mark. The pattern helps a specialist to work out the cause.
Once the colour has been treated, the stone needs protection.

1. Let the floor dry properly, as it may hold water for some time.
  2. Polish the treated area so that it matches the rest.
  3. Seal the stone with a suitable product.
  4. Change the routine that caused the stain, such as wet mopping.
Skipping any of these can bring the problem back.

Mop with very little water, use a pH-neutral cleaner, and keep mats that have rubber backing off the stone. Clean up rust and spills quickly. If you are not sure why the colour appeared, take a photo and send it to us. For a step-by-step home approach, read how to remove yellow stains from marble.

faqs.q: Can yellow marble be made white again?
faqs.a: Often it can be improved a lot, but it depends on the cause and the depth of the stain. We test a small area first.

faqs.q: Why did my floor turn yellow after polishing?
faqs.a: Too much water may have reached iron minerals in the stone, or a product may have reacted with it. Have it checked before you try another treatment.

faqs.q: Will bleach remove yellow stains from marble?
faqs.a: No. Bleach can damage the surface and rarely fixes the colour.

title: Etch Marks on Marble Countertops: Causes and Fixes
h1: Etch Marks on Marble Countertops: Causes, Fixes and Prevention
description: Dull rings on a marble countertop are usually etch marks. Learn how to tell them from stains, what fixes them and how to prevent them.
keywords: marble countertop polishing dubai in dubai
excerpt: Dull rings on a marble countertop are usually etch marks. Here is how to tell them from stains and how to fix them.
intro: You wipe your marble countertop, and a dull ring from a glass of juice stays behind. It looks like a water mark, but no amount of cleaning removes it. That is an etch mark, and it is the most common problem on marble kitchen tops. Here is what it is, how to deal with it, and how to prevent it.

body: Marble contains calcium carbonate, which reacts with acid. When lemon, vinegar, tomato, wine or even some cleaners touch the stone, the acid eats into the polished surface. That leaves a dull patch that looks paler than the rest of the top.
They need different treatment, so check which you have.

• An etch mark looks dull or pale, and you can see it best in the light.
  • A stain looks darker, because a liquid has soaked into the stone.
  • An oil stain fades a little and then returns, and it usually sits near the hob.

sections.h2: How to deal with etch marks
body: Light etching on a polished top can sometimes be improved with a marble polishing paste made for home use. Follow the label and test a hidden spot first. Results vary, and rubbing too hard can leave a patch.

Deeper marks need professional polishing. A technician uses fine diamond pads to remove a very thin layer, and then brings the shine back. If you have a lot of rings, it is usually better to polish the whole top so the finish stays even.
Stains need a poultice, which is a paste that draws the liquid out of the stone. It often takes more than one treatment. Do not use bleach or acid on it, as you may swap a stain for an etch mark.

• Use coasters for drinks and trays for oils and vinegar.
  • Cut lemons and tomatoes on a board.
  • Wipe up spills straight away.
  • Clean with a pH-neutral stone cleaner.
  • Keep bathroom and glass cleaners off the top.
Sealing helps with stains, but it does not stop acid. That surprises many owners. A sealed marble top can still etch.

sections.h2: Would a honed finish be better?
body: Etch marks are easiest to see on a glossy surface. A honed, satin finish hides them much better, which is why many busy kitchens use it. If you are tired of the marks, ask about changing the finish when you next polish the top.

sections.h2: How to test your top for etch marks and stains
body: You can check most marks with two simple tests.

• Wipe the mark with a damp cloth. A stain often looks darker when wet, while etching usually looks the same.
  • Tilt your head so the light hits the surface at a low angle. Etching appears as a dull shape. A stain appears as a colour.
If you have both, deal with the stain first, and polish afterwards. Polishing first can trap the stain, and a poultice can dull a polished surface.

sections.h2: Foods and products that cause most marks
body: These are the usual causes in a UAE kitchen.

• Lemon, lime and tamarind.
  • Tomato sauce, vinegar and pickles.
  • Yoghurt, wine, coffee and fizzy drinks.
  • Oven cleaner and bathroom sprays.
  • Ketchup bottles and cooking oil left standing on the surface.
A small tray next to the hob for oil, vinegar and salt solves many of these problems.

sections.h2: How often should you polish a top?
body: There is no fixed rule. It depends on how you cook and how much the marks bother you. Some families polish every couple of years. Others accept light marks as part of living with marble and only call when the top looks tired. Water that soaks in quickly tells you that it is time to reseal, even if polishing can wait.

• Using a shop-bought paste on a honed top. It can leave a shiny patch.
  • Rubbing a mark with baking soda paste for a long time. It is mildly abrasive.
  • Using a scouring pad around the sink.
  • Polishing only one spot on a glossy top. It may not match the rest.
If the marks are close to your sink, check that the tap and the seal are not leaking. Regular dripping can damage the same spot again.
Call us if the marks cover a large area, if the top feels rough, or if water soaks in quickly. Our marble countertop polishing service removes etching and reseals the stone with the top in place.

faqs.q: Can etch marks be removed permanently?
faqs.a: Yes. Polishing removes the damaged layer, but new acid spills can leave new marks.

faqs.q: Does sealing stop etching?
faqs.a: No. Sealing slows stains, but acid can still react with the surface.

faqs.q: Why do marks show more in some light?
faqs.a: Etching changes how the surface reflects light, so side lighting and under-cabinet lights make it easier to see.

title: Why Emperador Marble Shows Every Mark, and What Helps
h1: Why Emperador Marble Shows Every Mark, and What Helps
description: Dark Emperador marble shows water spots, scratches and dust. Learn why it happens and how to keep this brown stone looking rich.
excerpt: Dark Emperador marble shows water spots, scratches and dust. Here is why it happens and what helps.
intro: Emperador looks rich and warm when it is clean and polished. It can also feel like hard work, because every water spot, fingerprint and scratch stands out on the dark surface. If you own this stone, the right habits make a big difference. Here is what causes the marks, and what you can do about each one.

body: Light marks stand out against dark stone. Dust, soap film and water spots are all pale, so they show far more on Emperador than on a cream marble. The stone also has white veins, which can wear differently from the brown areas around them.
That does not mean that Emperador is weak. It just means that you notice wear sooner.
White marks are the most common complaint, and they come in two kinds.

• Water deposits sit on top of the stone. You can often feel them with a fingernail.
  • Etch marks are part of the surface. They look dull, and they feel smooth or slightly rough.
To test a mark, wipe it with a damp cloth and dry it. If it fades while it is wet and then returns, it may be etching or wear. Deposits around taps usually build up in layers.

Sand and grit cause most of the wear. On a dark floor, the scratches turn grey and make the stone look faded. You can slow this down with mats and regular dust-mopping, but once the floor looks grey, it needs professional polishing.
Emperador is popular in bathrooms, but water and soap are hard on it. These habits help.

• Wipe vanities and shower walls dry after use.
  • Use a soft squeegee on large surfaces.
  • Keep soap, shampoo and perfume on a tray.
  • Avoid bathroom sprays that contain acid or bleach.
Check the joints around showers as well. Water behind the stone can leave marks that polishing cannot fix.

A polisher removes deposits first, then uses diamond pads to take out scratches and dull areas. This brings back the deep brown colour. A colour-enhancing sealer can make the stone look a little darker if you like that look, but test it on a small area first.
You can read more about our Emperador marble polishing service.

sections.h2: Where to use Emperador, and where to take care
body: Emperador works well on feature walls, vanities, stair treads and hallways with good lighting. It needs more attention in these places.

• Near entrances, where sand scratches the surface and shows quickly.
  • On kitchen tops, where acidic food can leave pale marks.
  • In showers, where water and soap dry into spots.
  • Under strong side lighting, which picks out every scratch.
If you are planning a new home, think about the light as well as the stone. Soft lighting from above is kinder than a strong beam across the floor.

Dark marble shows residue, so choose a cleaner that rinses clean. A pH-neutral stone cleaner with no added wax is the best option. Use only a little, as too much leaves streaks. Avoid milky shine products, which can leave a pale film on dark stone.
Rinse your mop often. A dirty mop spreads grit and leaves a dull haze. Microfibre mops work well, as long as they are clean.

Polished Emperador shows the deep brown colour and the white veins clearly, but it also shows every mark. A honed finish looks softer and hides wear better, though the colour looks lighter. A colour-enhancing sealer can bring back some depth on a honed surface. Test any option on a small area first, as the look can change a lot.

• Leaving water to air-dry on a vanity.
  • Using a limescale remover on marks around taps. These products contain acid and can leave a pale ring.
  • Using abrasive powder on water spots.
  • Waxing the floor to hide scratches.
If limescale builds up around a tap, use a plastic scraper gently, and ask a professional to treat it.

• Dust-mop floors, preferably every day.
  • Clean with a pH-neutral stone cleaner.
  • Dry the surface with a soft cloth to avoid streaks.
  • Check for new marks around taps and basins.
A dry finish matters on this stone. Air-dried water leaves spots, while a quick buff with a clean cloth leaves the surface clear.

faqs.q: How do I remove water spots from Emperador?
faqs.a: Try a pH-neutral stone cleaner and a soft cloth. If the spots stay, they may be hard deposits or etch marks, which need professional work.

faqs.q: Can scratches be polished out of Emperador?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Fine scratches come out with diamond polishing. Deep scratches need more stone removal, or a filler.

faqs.q: Is Emperador good for a bathroom?
faqs.a: Yes, if you keep it dry and seal it. It does need more wiping than a lighter stone to stay free of marks.

title: Why Crema Marfil Turns Dull or Patchy, and How to Fix It
h1: Why Crema Marfil Floors Turn Dull or Patchy, and How to Fix It
description: Crema Marfil floors often turn dull, patchy or orange. Learn the common causes in UAE homes and which fixes work for each one.
keywords: crema marfil marble polishing dubai in
excerpt: Crema Marfil floors often turn dull, patchy or orange. Here are the common causes in UAE homes and the fixes that work.
intro: Crema Marfil is everywhere in the UAE, from villa halls to apartment bathrooms. Its soft cream colour looks calm and warm when it is new, but after a few years many owners notice dull paths, darker patches or an orange tone. Each of these has a different cause, so the fix depends on what you see.

body: This is the most common problem. Sand on shoes acts like sandpaper and wears the polish away from hallways, doorways and the space around sofas. The stone is not dirty. Its surface is simply scratched.
Cleaning will not bring the shine back. The floor needs honing and polishing to take out the fine scratches.
Crema Marfil is porous. If water gets under or into the tile, you may see darker areas, often near bathrooms, kitchens or external doors. These patches can come and go as the stone dries.
First find the source of the water. Polishing will not help until the leak or damp has been dealt with.

Old wax, strong cleaners and minerals in the stone can all change its colour. Wax is the easiest to check. If the colour sits in a sticky or uneven film, a stripper may lift it. If the colour is inside the stone, you will need a specialist treatment.
Read more about the causes in our guide on why marble turns yellow.

Crema Marfil has natural veins and fissures, and factories often fill them with resin. Over time, the filler can wear away and leave small gaps that collect dirt. A polisher should fill these gaps before the final polish, using a colour-matched filler.

If you can feel an edge with your foot, the tiles are not level. This is called lippage. Those edges chip, catch dirt and show up in the light. Grinding flattens the floor, but it is a bigger job, so ask whether your floor really needs it.

• Dull paths: honing and polishing.
  • Damp patches: find the water first, then assess the stone.
  • Wax build-up: strip it, then polish.
  • Deep colour change: test a specialist treatment on a small area.
  • Open veins: fill, then polish.
  • Raised edges: grind, then polish.
We can check your floor and tell you which of these apply. See our Crema Marfil polishing service for more detail.

sections.h2: How to check your own floor
body: You can learn a lot in a few minutes.

1. Look across the floor at a low angle, with light from a window. Dull paths and scratches will show up.
  2. Run your hand across the joints. Raised edges mean lippage.
  3. Check the darkest patches near bathrooms and doors. Touch them to see if they feel damp.
  4. Scrape a hidden corner gently with a plastic card. If a film lifts, you may have wax.
  5. Drip some water on the stone. If it soaks in quickly, the floor needs sealing.
Take photos of what you find. They help a stone company give you a better first answer.

sections.h2: Why bathrooms and kitchens suffer first
body: Water is the main reason. Showers can push water into joints, and the stone around them may turn darker. Kitchens add oil, which leaves dark stains, and cleaning sprays, which leave dull areas. Check the joints and silicone around these rooms before you plan any polishing.

sections.h2: What polishing can and cannot do
body: Polishing is very good at removing scratches, dull paths and light etching. It cannot remove colour that goes deep into the stone, and it will not fix a floor that is still damp. It also cannot repair loose or hollow tiles. If you tap a tile and it sounds hollow, ask for it to be checked first.
An honest company will show you a small test area on a difficult floor. That way, you can see the likely result before you pay for the whole job.

sections.h2: Mistakes that make Crema Marfil worse
body:
• Mopping with too much water.
  • Using bleach to lighten dark patches.
  • Applying wax to hide dullness.
  • Using a steam mop.
  • Sealing a damp floor, which can trap the moisture.
If you have tried one of these, tell the technician. It changes the way they will approach the floor.
Use mats at the doors, dust-mop daily and clean with a pH-neutral cleaner. Avoid soaking the floor with a wet mop. Too much water is a common cause of patches on this stone.

faqs.q: Can polishing fix orange marks on Crema Marfil?
faqs.a: Only if the colour is on the surface. Deeper colour needs a stain treatment, and it may improve rather than disappear.

faqs.q: Why does my floor look darker after mopping?
faqs.a: The stone is absorbing water. It should lighten as it dries. If it stays dark, the floor may need sealing, or water may be getting in from below.

faqs.q: Should I seal Crema Marfil?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. A sealer slows down spills and helps with cleaning, especially in kitchens and bathrooms.
